description: The humans worship a triune divine -- three personalities in one form: the Father, the Mother, and the Child. In their world there are two kinds of magic, and their strength is inverted from what one might expect. Wizardry (learned, arcane) is feeble -- the stuff of parlor tricks, street scams, and charlatans. FAITH-based magic, drawn from the triune god, is extremely strong and genuinely real. The kingdom's true wonders are all faith-wrought.
rules: Faith-magic vastly outstrips wizardry; it is literal, reliable, and sacred. Two faith-workings matter most to this story: the bond-stone (soul-mate detection and, in matrimony, a literal soul-bond) and the knight's oath (a ritual faith-binding with real metaphysical force). Because faith-magic is real, a broken faith-oath is not merely a social disgrace -- it carries an actual mystical price.

details.The Triune (Father / Mother / Child): One god in three persons. Domains provisional: Father -- law, protection, the keeping of oaths; Mother -- life, mercy, healing; Child -- renewal, change, hope (and perhaps the unforeseen). Refine as needed.
details.Wizardry: Arcane, learned magic -- weak and disreputable. Widely dismissed as parlor tricks or used to run scams. A wizard commands no real power beside a faith-worker.
details.Faith-magic: The strong, true magic, sourced in devotion to the triune god. Rare and precious; its practitioners and instruments are trusted where wizards are mocked.
details.Bond-stones: A faith-worked stone given to every human in the kingdom at age eight. When a person and their true soul-mate clasp hands upon it together, it glows brightly -- the god's confirmation of a matched pair. To lose one's bond-stone is regarded as gravely as losing one's own life. In matrimony the stone becomes a conduit for a literal SOUL-BOND: two souls joined so that they share everything -- skills, sensations, experiences. A profound intimacy and a profound vulnerability.
details.The knight's oath: A knight is made by a ritual faith-binding sworn before the triune god -- real magic, an oath with metaphysical teeth. It is the human echo of the same sacred order that damned the dragonkin: to be forsworn is to be unmade. Proposed price: breaking the oath undoes what it made -- the forsworn knight loses the faith-granted standing, strength, and blessing that raised him, and is marked as oathbreaker in the sight of god and men. For a low-born knight who owes everything to the oath, this is a return to nothing. (Exact price to confirm.)
details.The bond-stone and the dragonkin (CANON): A human's bond-stone DOES glow for the dragonkin woman. Though she has no part in the triune faith and bears no stone of her own, when she and the knight clasp hands upon his stone together it blazes -- the god's own magic naming her his true soul-mate, the one person his faith's law forbids him. The divine affirms the love the divine's kingdom condemns. Because the working requires both hands on the stone, the revelation is necessarily an intimate, deliberate act between them.
details.The knight's stone (character seed): As a young man the knight loved deeply and was loved in return; he and she meant to bond for life. But their stones never glowed for one another. He took the lesson that love and the god's sanction do not always align, tucked that part of himself away, and gave his years to the oath instead -- until, against all he had come to believe, the stone blazes for the dragonkin. (Belongs to his character file at Characters stage.)
details.Open / to confirm: The Triune's exact domains; the precise price of a broken knight's oath; whether a human-dragonkin soul-bond can actually be forged in matrimony -- and what it would mean to share, through the bond, the experience of the curse.
